title: Extracting duplicated retry logic into a shared module
notes: Refactor session with a deliberate 'noticed but deferred' decision, to test whether extractors capture both the action taken AND the explicit non-action.

turns.text: The retry logic for HTTP calls is duplicated in three provider files (ollama.ts, azure-openai.ts, and the embed providers). Can we extract it?
Yes — I'll pull the shared fetchWithRetry logic into a new src/providers/lib/fetch-retry.ts module and have all four providers import it instead of each having their own copy.
Make sure the retry behavior stays identical — same timeout, same no-retry-on-4xx rule.

Confirmed: extracted with the same signature (url, init, timeoutMs), same rules — no retry on 4xx, one retry on 5xx or network error/timeout. All four call sites now import the shared version; ran the existing provider tests and they pass unchanged.
Good. Any other duplication you noticed while you were in there?

Yes — all four providers also independently build a childLogger({provider, model}) at the top of chat(). That's smaller, I'd leave it for a separate pass since it's low-risk duplication, not worth the churn right now.
Agreed, leave that one. Ship the retry extraction.

gold_atoms.text: Extract the duplicated fetchWithRetry logic (present in ollama.ts, azure-openai.ts, and the embed providers) into a shared src/providers/lib/fetch-retry.ts module.
The shared retry logic preserves identical behavior: no retry on 4xx, one retry on 5xx or network error/timeout, same (url, init, timeoutMs) signature.
All four provider call sites were switched to import the shared fetchWithRetry; existing provider tests pass unchanged.
Leave the childLogger({provider, model}) duplication across the four providers alone for now — smaller, low-risk, not worth the churn in this refactor.
